intro: Ohio runs elections through its 88 county boards of elections, with the Secretary of State overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Bring a photo ID that is not expired and shows your name, such as an Ohio driver's license or state ID, interim ID from the Ohio BMV, U.S. passport or passport card, U.S. military ID, Ohio National Guard ID, or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs ID.

dates.label: Early in-person voting
dates.detail: Vote at your county board of elections. Days and hours differ by county. In Franklin County, weekday hours are longer in the last week, and the last day is Sunday, Nov. 1.

src.label: Franklin County (OH) Board of Elections, absentee voting

dates.label: Last day to request an absentee ballot
dates.detail: Your county board of elections must receive your application by 8:30 pm. No excuse is needed.

src.label: Franklin County (OH) Board of Elections, absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6:30 am to 7:30 pm. An absentee ballot must be received by your county board of elections by 7:30 pm.
